correctness.rationale: For all binary sequences, direct-sum Jacobi path spectra give the exact radius. If exactly one finite maximal run exists, its sine eigenvector is a simple top eigenvector with a uniform positive spectral gap from the rest. A Rayleigh-quotient perturbation estimate controls the nonlinear modulus map at zero weights to quadratic order, yielding the displayed real Fréchet derivative. In case of tied finite maxima, perturbing one maximal run gives unequal one-sided slopes. In case of unbounded runs, disjoint families of arbitrarily long one-blocks produce a direction h with N(a+th)=1+|t|. The zero sequence is a norm singularity. No finite check is used as an infinite proof. The nonstandard spectral-gap estimate is reproduced in RESULT with its Rayleigh decomposition.

value.rationale: Binary sequences are the vertices of the positive coordinate cube and select precisely the path components of the underlying Jacobi graph, so this is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem identifies the exact transition between a unique finite dominating component, ties, and arbitrarily long components, gives the exact infinite-family norm and a nontrivial unrestricted complex perturbation derivative, and covers infinite-support sequences excluded by simple finite-matrix statements.
